Misc. Appeal No. 1335 of 2009
 Mahila Phoolwati And Others
 Versus
 Shailendra Thapak And Others

Appearance:
 Shri B.D.Verma - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri Shrinivas Gajendragadkar- Advocate for the respo

Order 
This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicle Act has been filed against award dated 24/07/2009 passed by Fourth Additional Member, MACT, Morena in MACC No.260/2007.
2.

It is not out of place to mention here that against the same award, insurance company had also filed M.A.No.1485/2009 and by a separate order passed today, the principle of pay and recover applied by Claims Tribunal has been upheld.
3.
The present appeal has been filed by the widow, two minor children, father, mother and sister of the deceased Dhaniram, who was aged about 26 years.
Since, the factum of accident is not in dispute, therefore, it is suffice to mention here that deceased Dhaniram met with a vehicular accident on 06/08/2007 at about 7:30 PM and lost his life.

It was the case that the driver of jeep bearing registration No. MP07-GA-0654 turned jeep turtle by driving NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28092 2 MA-1335-2009 the same in rash and negligent manner, as a result,
deceased Dhaniram who was standing by the side got crashed under the jeep and died on the spot.

4. It is submitted by counsel for appellants that Claims Tribunal has taken the notional annual income of deceased as Rs.15,000/-, but as per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly wages of an unskilled labourer were Rs.2,602/- and, therefore, yearly income of deceased should have been taken as Rs.31,224/-.
It is further submitted that since, the deceased was Mahila Phoolwati vs Shailendra Thapak on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90779192/
1 survived by his widow, two children as well as his mother also, therefore, Claims Tribunal should have taken personal expenses as 1/4.
It is further submitted that compensation amount awarded under other conventional heads is also on a lower side.
5 . Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by counsel for respondent No.3.

However, it was fairly conceded that personal expenses should have been taken as 1/4 instead of 1/3.
6.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

7. It is well established principle of law that where claimants of the deceased have failed to prove the notional income of deceased, then notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act can be taken as a guiding factor.
As per the notification issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly wages of an unskilled labourer were Rs.2,602/-.
Accordingly, monthly income of deceased is taken as Rs.2,602/-.
Legal representatives are also entitled for future prospect, and the widow, two minor children and mother of the deceased are also entitled for consortium.

8. Accordingly, appellants No.1 to 3 and 5 are entitled for following NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-GWL:28092 3 MA-1335-2009 compensation amount:-
Monthly Income of the deceased   Yearly Income of the deceased   Personal Expenses (1/4)
Yearly loss of yearly dependency

Total loss of dependency after applying the multiplier of 17 3,98,106/-
 Future prospects (40%)
Loss of estate   Funeral expenses

Consortium (40,000 x 4) 
 Total amount   Compensation awarded by Claims Tribunal   Compensation amount enhanced by  Accordingly, the compensation amount is enhanced by a further sum of Rs.5,65,848/-.
Remaining conditions of award shall remain the same.
Ex-consequenti, with aforesaid modification, the award dated 24/07/2009 passed by Fourth Additional Member, MACT, Morena in MACC No.260/2007 is hereby affirmed.
Appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed.

(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE PjS/-
